text:
Ravi: heads-up — pushed v1.17.0 of the JS SDK with a more specific exports map to tidy up browser vs node entrypoints. now the react-native/metro sample crashes during bundling: 

Tess: oh no — what error do you see?

Ravi: Metro fails with: `Unable to resolve module '@redwood-inference/sdk' from /app/App.js: Module does not exist in the module map` even though node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk exists.

Olivia: metro/packagers don't fully implement Node conditional exports resolution and also prefer .react-native or browser fields. what did the new package.json exports look like?

Ravi: here's the relevant part we shipped:
```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs.js",
      "node": "./dist/node/index.cjs.js",
      "default": "./dist/esm/index.mjs"
    },
    "./browser": "./dist/browser/index.mjs"
  },
  "main": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "browser": "./dist/browser/index.mjs"
}
```

Tess: two likely issues: 1) metro doesn't resolve conditional exports keys like "default"/"node" and may ignore the package entirely if it sees an exports map it can't parse, 2) our ESM exports don't guarantee a default export so `import sdk from` in some samples will break.

Olivia: plus TypeScript projects that rely on `paths` or older packagers will try to read `main` or `browser` first. mixing `browser` and `exports` can be surprising.

Ravi: repro steps I used: clone `samples/react-native`, `yarn install`, `yarn react-native start` -> metro errors out. CI also flagged sample-packaging job.

CI Bot: sample/react-native packaging check failed on release: `Error: Unable to resolve module '@redwood-inference/sdk' from '/workspace/samples/react-native/App.js'`

Tess: quick mitigation options: revert exports to previous conditional map that only had import/require and keep `browser` top-level, or add a `react-native` subpath like "./react-native": "./dist/react-native/index.js". Revert is fastest.

Ravi: I'm going to cut 1.17.1 reverting the exports changes to unblock consumers.

Olivia: long-term we should: add a small compatibility matrix (Node, browsers, react-native/metro, deno, cloudflare workers), produce a tiny `dist/react-native` build that uses CommonJS-ish shape Metro expects, and ensure our ESM build exports a `default` (or document `import * as SDK`). Also add `react-native` or `main` fallback in exports so bundlers without full conditional exports still find something.

Tess: also add a unit that validates package.json exposures during CI: a script that runs `resolve.exports` style checks against a matrix of runtimes and flags unsupported patterns.

Docs Bot: drafting docs PR for "Packaging and exports: Edge, React Native, and Bundlers" with examples and recommended patterns. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/475

Release Bot: published v1.17.1 reverting exports to prior conditional map. samples/react-native checks are now passing.

Ravi: thanks. I'll follow up with a ticket to implement the compat builds and CI matrix and ping @Tess/@Olivia to design the smoke tests.

Tess: small UX note for SDK maintainers checklist: whenever changing `exports`/`main`/`browser` add a one-line hint in the PR description: "ran samples: node, browser, deno, react-native? yes/no". helps reviewers. :memo:
